messages:
ivy: Heads-up — while onboarding harbor-32k int4 I hit a pretty odd wraparound/ghost-token case. Prefill length sits right below the shard window (window_size=16384, prefill_len=16320). Flow: prefill (~16.32k), append (~2k), resume streaming. Intermittent small ghost sequence (2-4 toks) that mirror tokens from prefill tail. Repro ~1/220.

noah: Which pool and policy? Any short logs we can peek at?

ivy: perf-lab pl-11, kv_policy=fold. Quick failing excerpt: 

```
[cache] prefill id=0x6d3a fp=0xabc1 len=16320 slot=0 epoch=7
[cache] append id=0x6d3b fp=0xabc2 len+=2048 slot=0 epoch=7
stitcher: computed_split_idx=16320 shard_wrap_check=true
gen: step=16321 token=1293 ghost_detected idx=16318-16321
[cache] post_fp=0xabc2 != expected_fp=0xabc1
```

priya: Huh. "shard_wrap_check=true" is interesting. Could be an off-by-window stride where we cross the internal ring buffer wrap and the posshift math subtracts a window incorrectly. Any per-layer ropechecks?

ivy: I added a tiny per-layer ropecheck that computes a 64-bit rolling xor of the sin/cos pair after stitch; failing trace shows mismatch only on layers [10,11] (adjacent middle layers). That feels like a layer-indexing slip rather than global rebase.

marc: Two ideas to triage: 1) try forcing `stitcher.window_normalize=false` to avoid subtracting window_size in the offset math (cheap toggle) and 2) instrument last-128-kv-word xor hash before and after append to assert atomicity. If xor before != xor after and we didn't reset, suspect ordering/race.

noah: Also consider quantization accumulation noise: int4 kernels sometimes reorder multiply-adds per-lane; if a per-layer posscale clamp runs slightly different rounding on appended segment, the ropecalc checksum can drift and appear as ghosting. Try running with float fallback for the suspected layers as an experiment.

priya: Another low-overhead probe: add a tiny `stitch-sanity` check that simulates applying the computed posshift to a short synthetic suffix and compares logits with a reference single-request run. If difference > epsilon, emit a debug snapshot and fail the fold (fall back to reset for that request). We can make it opt-in for perf debugging.

ivy: I ran the floating fallback on layers 10..12 for 10k iterations; ghost disappeared in that subset of runs. So either rounding/order in quant kernel or a subtle index mismatch that float arithmetic masks.

marc: Good signal. Next step: reproduce deterministically with seeded RNG in qemu-int4 across both x86 and arm64. If arm64 amplifies rate it's likely an ordering/membar issue. Also capture raw slot dumps (keys + per-layer pos offsets) on fail.

noah: Small nit: when prefill_len is close to window boundary we may end up with `computed_split_idx = prefix_len - window_size` in some code paths (negative wrap) and we guard by `if (split_idx < 0) split_idx += window_size` but there's a place where we index `layer_offset = split_idx + layer_stride` without re-normalizing per-layer; that could hit the wrong slot for middle layers. Worth auditing the stitcher index normalization carefully.

priya: I'll add a unit test that brute-forces prefix_len values around 16k boundary (16360..16384) and runs the 2-request flow 100k times to collect frequency vs prefix_len. If we see a spike exactly at 16320 that's revealing.

ci-bot: Created issue #5780: "harbor-32k: wraparound ghost tokens at shard boundary under kv_fold" (reporter: ivy) :mag:

marc: If kernel rounding is part of it, we should also try an alternate quant backend (int4v2 vs int4v1) on the same node to isolate kernel ordering differences. If float fallback eliminates it but alternate int4 kernel still reproduces, it's a kernel bug.

ivy: I've got the brute-force harness going and a branch with: (A) window_normalize toggle, (B) float-fallback for layers 9..13, (C) per-layer ropecheck XOR + slot-xor assertion. Running 100k seeded iterations on both archs. Uploading artifacts to /artifacts/harbor32k/3135792000.tar.gz.

noah: If we can make a cheap per-request failover (stitch-sanity) that catches the minority of bad folds and falls back to reset, that might be an acceptable stopgap until we fix root cause. Falling back costs ~18-22ms but if it's <0.5% of requests overall SLO still fine.

priya: Agree. We'll aim for detection-first hotfix (stitch-sanity) + root-cause triage (index normalization audit + kernel comparison).

ivy: I'll post results tomorrow. TL;DR: ghost tokens near shard boundary, finger prints change post-append, float fallback reduces occurrence, running deterministic sweep to isolate index vs kernel root cause. :eyes:
